summary: End-to-end testing of the R-backed Reproducible Research Console. Backend: 10/10 pytest tests pass against public URL — /api/health reports R 4.2.2 and packages_ok, POST /api/analysis/run shells out to Rscript (exit 0), /api/analysis/results returns the real parsed R tables (raw_rows=1020, cleaned_rows=1000, duplicate_rows_removed=20, 3 key_correlations, correlation matrix, previews), POST /api/tests/run returns passed=true with real testthat output, all 4 figures return valid PNG bytes, dataset downloads (raw & clean) return CSV. Frontend: dashboard loads, validation badges populated from live API (1020 / 171 / 20 / 24 / 10 / 10), correlation matrix grid renders real r/p values, 4 ggplot2 PNGs load in figures-gallery-grid, Run R Analysis button triggers backend and refreshes results, Run tests button shows 'All tests passed' with real R console output in r-console-output-terminal, theme toggle switches dark/light, rmarkdown-report-link points to /api/report. All features work genuinely (not hardcoded).
action_items: Minor: review-request mentioned data-testids 'stat-raw-rows / stat-missing-cells / stat-duplicate-rows / stat-invalid-entries' but implementation uses 'raw-row-count / missing-values-badge / duplicates-count-badge / invalid-entries-badge'. Functionality is correct and badges render real values; only the testid naming diverges from the spec. Decide whether to rename or update the spec.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is clean, uses async routes and subprocess shell-out to Rscript with timeout and proper HTTPException mapping. No MongoDB used (file-based R outputs), no _id leak risk.
CORS allow_credentials=True with default allow_origins='*' — browsers reject that combo; harmless here since no auth cookies are used, but worth tightening.
No input validation on /api/dataset/download?which=... — silently falls back to clean for any value other than 'raw'. Consider enum/Pydantic validation.
/api/report returns HTML via PlainTextResponse with media_type override — works but using HTMLResponse would be more idiomatic.
seed_data_creation: Not required — the R pipeline deterministically generates the synthetic dataset (set.seed in R).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend regression suite at /app/backend/tests/test_r_pipeline.py (10 tests, ~8s). Frontend testids actually in use: raw-row-count, missing-values-badge, duplicates-count-badge, invalid-entries-badge, inconsistent-gender-badge, inconsistent-quality-badge, correlation-matrix-grid, key-corr-{i}, p-value-badge-{i}, figures-gallery-grid, run-r-pipeline-button, run-tests-button, r-console-output-terminal, theme-toggle-button, rmarkdown-report-link, r-engine-status, download-raw-button, download-clean-button.
